title: Shift orchestration and status canvas
author: Marcus Liang
content:
Overview

This page documents the Shift Orchestration pattern and the Status Canvas: a lightweight, modular approach to on-call handoffs, live incident status updates, and customer-facing messages. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incident windows, accelerate safe stabilization, and produce consistent artifacts for post-incident review.

Scope and audience
- Audience: first/second-line responders, incident commanders, bridge operators, on-call engineers, SRE leads, customer success when escalation is active.
- Scope: active incident lifecycle (ack -> contain -> stabilize -> restore -> retrospective) and the handoff/state model used inside and across shifts.

Key principles
1. Minimal, shared state: handoffs must surface only the essential facts (impact, hypothesis, next action, blockers).
2. Modular status text: compose updates from reusable sentence fragments (the Status Canvas) to avoid inconsistent messaging under pressure.
3. Timeboxed cadence: fixed checkpoints (10m, 30m, 60m, then hourly) for internal and external updates.
4. Champion ownership: a named Incident Commander (IC) owns the public narrative; the bridge operator owns the timeline/triage log.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): owns decision-making, public status updates, escalation decisions.
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge, posts comms to Slack/status page, maintains triage log.
- Primary Responder: works contained area (service, model, infra).
- Secondary/Support: deeper debug, infra changes, runbook actions.
- Customer Liaison (CS/Success): owns customer-specific comms where required and ensures SLA/regulatory notes.

Shift handoff checklist (state canvas)
For every rotation, leave a single-line subject and a structured canvas in the handoff channel or incident tracker. Required fields:
1) Active incident? (yes/no)
2) Incident ID(s) / Bridge link (URL)
3) Impact summary (1 sentence)
4) Current hypothesis and known mitigations
5) Actions in-flight and authors (command + ETA)
6) Blockers / resource needs
7) Followup / post-incident actions due to next shift

Example handoff (paste into #oncall-handoffs):
- Active incident: yes
- Bridge: https://meet.example/bridge/INC-2026-137
- Impact: API 503s for embedding endpoints in us-west; estimated 65% of customer requests failing.
- Hypothesis: model cache eviction + rate limiter misconfiguration causing backend queue overflows.
- Actions: rolling cache-size increase (alice) — ETA 12m; temporary QPS cap (bob) — completed.
- Blockers: capacity for canary pool exhausted; infra request filed (#1234).
- Next shift notes: continue cache monitor for 30m post-rollout; begin RCA prep.

Incident lifecycle: step-by-step
1. Acknowledge (T+0–10m)
  - Pager duty: responder acknowledges within 5 minutes.
  - Bridge is stood up and pinned in #incident-bridge.
  - IC and Bridge Operator are declared in the first 10 minutes.
  - First internal status posted to internal channel.
2. Triage & containment (T+10–30m)
  - Run the relevant containment runbook. See quick links below.
  - If customer-impacting, prepare a short external status (see Status Canvas fragments).
3. Stabilize (T+30–90m)
  - Apply mitigations and monitor key SLOs (latency, error-rate, successful tokens).
  - If mitigation fails, escalate to platform/infra and consider fallback model variant.
4. Restore & validate (T+90–240m)
  - Run smoke tests and validate end-to-end flows.
  - Update customers and close bridge when validated.
5. Retrospective (post-incident)
  - Collect timeline, artifacts, logs, config diffs, and runbook versions.
  - IC ensures postmortem draft within 72 hours; final review within 14 days.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
| Metric | Alert threshold | Initial action | Owner |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| API error rate (5m) | > 5% | Pager to pager-team | svc-owner |
| Tail latency (p95) | > 1.5s | Notify oncall | oncall-responder |
| Embedding 503 rate | > 3% | Bridge & start triage | IC |

Communications: the Status Canvas
The Status Canvas is a set of modular sentence fragments that are combined to form consistent updates. Use the minimal appropriate fragments for brevity. 

Fragments — Impact level (choose one):
- minor: "A subset of requests are experiencing increased latency; no customer-facing errors observed."
- elevated: "Some customers may see errors or degraded responses; a remediation is in progress."
- critical: "A significant portion of traffic is failing; we have opened an incident and are actively working to restore service."

Fragments — Action (choose one):
- investigating: "Our team is investigating the root cause and collecting logs and traces."
- mitigating: "We are applying mitigations (temporary routing and capacity adjustments) to limit impact."
- rolling-back: "We are rolling back the most recent configuration change to restore baseline behavior."
- fallback: "We are routing affected requests to a compatible model variant while we resolve the primary issue."

Fragments — ETA / next update (choose one):
- eta-10m: "Expect an update in ~10 minutes."
- eta-30m: "Expect an update in ~30 minutes as we validate mitigations."
- eta-hourly: "We will provide hourly updates until resolution."

External status templates (examples)
- Initial external (elevated/critical):
  "[Time UTC] Status: {impact-fragment} {action-fragment} {eta-fragment} We will provide updates via this status page and direct customer messages as appropriate. (Incident ID: INC-2026-137)"

- Follow-up / Resolution:
  "[Time UTC] Update: service behavior has returned to baseline following {short-action-summary}. We are monitoring for recurrence and will publish a post-incident summary within 14 days. (Incident ID: INC-2026-137)"

Channel and cadence guidance
- Internal bridge channel: #incident-bridge-{id} (private) — use for operational chatter, temporary config commands, and triage logs.
- Public status page: update at T+30m for customer-visible incidents and then hourly.
- Customer notices: CS owns targeted emails or account-level notices; IC approves the message.
- Slack posting template (bridge operator):
  "INC-2026-137 — {short-impact} — {link to status} — IC: @user — Next update: {time}"

Automation snippets (examples)
- curl JSON payload to update our status service:
  curl -X POST https://status.redwood.example/api/v1/incidents \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${STATUS_TOKEN}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"incident_id":"INC-2026-137","impact":"elevated","message":"We are mitigating increased errors for embeddings; expect update in 30m."}'

- PagerDuty escalation API example (short):
  curl -X POST https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents \
    -H 'Authorization: Token token=${PD_TOKEN}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"incident":{"type":"incident","title":"Embedding 503 spike","service":{"id":"PABC123"}}}'

Runbook references (quick links)
1. Embeddings 503 containment runbook — /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/embeddings-503-containment
2. KV cache eviction playbook — /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
3. Rate-limiter rollback SOP — /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/rate-limiter-rollback

Game day & run drills (recommended cadence)
- Quarterly: full multi-shift incident sim (4-hour exercise) with enforced handoffs and public status updates.
- Monthly: 90-minute targeted drills (e.g., cache eviction, model fallback).
- Post-drill: update runbooks and publish a one-page drill summary.

Artifacts required for post-incident review
- Complete triage timeline (timestamps, actor, actions)
- Runbook versions executed and diffs (commit IDs)
- Logs, traces, and sample request ids (anonymized if necessary)
- Status page messages and CS communications
- Short list of remediation and owners (owner + due date)

Handoff best practices (practical tips)
- Use the canvas template; avoid freeform — structured state reduces rework.
- Attach one validation screenshot or short metric chart showing pre/post mitigation effect.
- Mark any ongoing customer communications and pin the message to the channel.
- If escalation is pending (e.g., infra approval), include the request link and SLA for approval.

Appendix: short checklists
- Ten-minute checklist:
  1) Confirm bridge URL and participants.
  2) Define IC and Bridge Operator.
  3) Post brief internal status and triage hypothesis.
  4) Identify immediate mitigations.
- Handoff checklist (5 items):
  1) Bridge link and incident ID.
  2) Short impact sentence.
  3) Primary action in-flight and ETA.
  4) Blockers and required approvals.
  5) Next shift explicit owner.

Related pages and references
- Incident comm and postmortem framework — /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- First responder playbook — /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/first-responder-playbook-and-runbook-pruning-guidelines-2024

Ownership and review cadence
- Document owner: engineering / ops-runbook squad.
- Review cycle: quarterly or after any major incident exercise.

Contact and feedback
- For feedback or improvement proposals, open a PR against the runbook repo or ping #oncall-runbook-maintainers.
